prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: production sprite atlas for Cosmic: A Sea Beneath the Moon. Input image1 is a STYLE reference only: retain the medallion form, palette, grain and physical depiction approach, but create the NEW requested subjects below. Exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 circles total. Regular equal square cells, Use a SQUARE canvas, exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, equal square cells, no outer margin. Aim2048px wide. Every circle diameter84%of its cell, centred, with generous fully transparent gutters; leave allcells complete and separated. No extra cells or objects. Original astronomical chromolithograph with dry-gouache and chalk masses: deep indigo circular fields, feathered warm-ivory light, amber heat, copper/charcoal minerals and restrained teal water. Simplify to broad meaningful structures visible at72px. Fine grain stays in subjects; generous quiet dark space. One thin ivory circular outline. No glossy UI buttons, photographic lens flare, ornamental decoration, humans, machines, text, labels, numerals, formulas or grid lines. Inside each circle the field is opaque; outside circles true alpha transparency. No shadows, rays or fragments beyond circles. Atom/particle diagrams are schematic: tiny compact ivory dots and diffuse electron-probability clouds, never planetary electron orbits; individual nuclei do NOT glow like stars. Exact invisible chemistry is communicated by game names/readings, never by invented diagnostic coloration. All terrestrial worlds have bare mineral terrain; no plants, life or modern continents. Early Moon is pale gray-ivory without familiar dark maria. All Earth cutaways are views of one continuing world.
Strict row-major subjects (left to right, then top to bottom):
1. Rocky pebbles: Four compact rough dark pebbles with visibly granular edges, separated in a small group. Avoid: No pale ice mantles; less porous than the earlier loose aggregate.
2. Icy pebbles: Four rough dark-cored pebbles capped by uneven translucent ivory ice coatings. Avoid: Same pebble family with ice; no snowflakes or smooth miniature gas giants.
3. Drifting rocky pebbles: Three rocky pebbles staggered along a gently inward curved gas streamer with short trailing cues. Avoid: Movement along a route rather than dense accumulation.
4. A dense swarm of rocky solids: A compact curved crowd of small dark pebbles with sparse metal glints, gaps still visible. Avoid: Many separate solids, not one assembled sphere.
5. Rocky planetesimals: Two irregular substantial rocky bodies with rough faceted surfaces and a few nearby tiny grains for scale. Avoid: Bound larger bodies; no developed planetary layers or modern asteroid craters assumed.
6. An icy swarm concentrated by gas drag: A dense curved band of pale ice-coated pebbles interleaved with a faint gas flow, several small converging paths. Avoid: Collective concentration; no claim that only ice responds to this mechanism.
7. Icy planetesimals: Two irregular dark rocky bodies with pale ice-rich patches and a few tiny remaining grains. Avoid: Substantial bound objects; avoid pure white snowballs.
8. Heat from short-lived radionuclides: A rocky-body cutaway warms from sparse interior amber points spreading into a diffuse central glow. Avoid: Internal distributed heat source; no radiation trefoil or visible green radioactivity.
9. Collisions between small bodies: Two irregular small bodies collide at an edge and shed several angular fragments along diverging paths. Avoid: Rock fragments dominate, no planet-scale globe or giant fireball.
10. A melting rocky planetesimal: An irregular small body in cutaway shows dark exterior and glowing molten interior without settled layers. Avoid: Keep irregular small-body silhouette; no already formed metal core.
11. A hot, layered planetesimal: The same irregular body's wedge reveals a small copper-gray core beneath a thick hot silicate layer. Avoid: Still-hot mantle and irregular silhouette distinguish from cooler asteroid and round Earth.
12. A cooled differentiated asteroid: The same irregular cutaway asteroid has a dark solid outer shell and a small pale metallic interior. Avoid: No internal amber heat glow; retain its earlier outline and layer proportions.
13. Fragments of an asteroid core: Three angular metallic shards with broad copper-gray facets and sharp ivory edge glints. Avoid: Large representative broken core fragments, not microscopic grains or metal tools.
14. Fragments of an asteroid’s rocky layers: Three angular dark rock shards with dull fractured mineral faces, no metallic sheen. Avoid: Asteroid fragments in space; later coastal stones have water context.
15. Liquid water inside an icy body: An irregular ice-patched body cut away to reveal a confined teal liquid pocket against dark interior rock. Avoid: Liquid is internal and enclosed; no open planetary sea.
16. Water-bearing asteroid rock: A broken dark asteroid-rock sample with subdued altered mineral texture and one cutaway water-rock contact inset. Avoid: No water droplets leaking from hydrated minerals; bound hydrogen is not visibly blue.
